chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated to me, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd and his father Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah and Bukayr, the two sons of Aʿyan, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding the wiping: you wipe over the two sandals and do not insert your hand beneath the strap. And when you have wiped with some part of your head, or with some part of your feet from between the two ankles to the tips of the toes, then that has sufficed you.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: it sufficed you; it was legally adequate
key_terms.رَأْسِكَ: your head, the place of wiping in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.قَدَمَيْكَ: your two feet, the place of wiping in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about wiping the feet in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the manner of wiping in wudu (ablution), especially concerning wiping over the feet. It states that wiping over the footwear area is valid without placing the hand under the strap, and that wiping part of the head and part of the feet within the stated limits is sufficient.
